def _lens_basis_choices():
    """The warrants a writer may state: the column's own CHECK, minus `carried`, which only migration 131 writes."""
    return [v for v in (dbcore.schema_choices("extraction_lens_links", "basis") or []) if v != "carried"] or None


def _as_whole_words(text: str, field) -> bool:
    """`text` occurs in `field` on word boundaries, ignoring case (`e` is not in `the`)."""
    return bool(field) and re.search(r"(?<!\w)" + re.escape(text.lower()) + r"(?!\w)", field.lower()) is not None


def _saved_text_has(text: str, ref_id: str) -> bool:
    """`text` is in a file saved FOR `ref_id` (a scoped hit; a hit in another source's file proves nothing)."""
    return _retrieval_log().locate_quote(text, ref_id=ref_id)[0] == "scoped"


def _require_lens_warrant(conn, basis, basis_text, ref_id, claim_text, source_section, context,
                          basis_reason=None):
    """A link's warrant: a basis from the column's own CHECK (not `carried`) and the exact words that warrant it,
    which must be found on word boundaries, in the place the basis names:

      named_in_text       the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for its source (D-2: its own words name the users);
      heading             the figure's source_section, its own heading (OD-31);
      study_participants  the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for the source (2026-08-25);
      context             the figure's claim_text, its source_section, or a file saved for its source (the scope,
                          application or purpose clause): the words that state the clause's context, with
                          `basis_reason`, the recording session's judgment (OD-65; the sixteenth set of 2026-11-14,
                          as corrected 2026-11-15). Only on a source of tier 4 or above, the regulatory stratum: the
                          owner moved the assignment for code values only, so a research figure's group still comes
                          from its own words or its study's participants.

    `basis_reason` is given with `context` and with no other basis (a reason beside a stated warrant is a cell with no
    meaning). Returns (the stripped text, the stripped reason or None). WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHECK: that the words name
    the lens code itself. The registries
    do not hold a name for every code (about half the ICF d-codes have no title, access_needs has no name column), so a name test cannot be derived for them; whether the words name the group
    is the judge's (D-2) and the recorded warrant is what a later reader audits."""
    allowed = set(_lens_basis_choices() or ())
    if basis not in allowed:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: a lens link needs --lens-basis / --basis, one of {sorted(allowed)} (the warrant for "
            f"stating the figure in this group). Nothing was written.")
    reason = None if basis_reason is None else str(basis_reason).strip()
    if basis != "context" and reason is not None:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: a reason (--lens-basis-reason / --basis-reason) is the recording session's judgment and "
            f"belongs to basis `context` only; basis {basis} rests on the source's own words, so a reason beside it "
            f"would be a cell with no meaning. Nothing was written.")
    if basis == "context":
        tier = conn.execute("SELECT tier FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id=?", (ref_id,)).fetchone()
        if not (tier and tier[0] is not None and int(tier[0]) >= _REGULATORY_FROM_TIER):
            raise Refusal(
                f"{context}: basis `context` is for a code value (a source of tier 4 to 6); {ref_id} is tier "
                f"{tier[0] if tier else None}. The owner moved the contextual assignment of a lens to the recording "
                f"call for code values only (the sixteenth set, 2026-11-14: grep -n -F \"Owner instruction 2026-11-14 "
                f"(sixteenth set)\" references/project-standards.md); a research figure's group comes from its own "
                f"words (named_in_text, heading) or its study's participants. Nothing was written.")
        if not reason or not re.search(r"[^\W\d_]", reason):
            raise Refusal(
                f"{context}: basis `context` needs --lens-basis-reason / --basis-reason: your judgment, in words, "
                f"of why the clause's context warrants the link (for a mounting height: 'typically concerns "
                f"wheelchair users'). Nothing was written.")
    text = (basis_text or "").strip()
    if not text:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant's words are blank. Give --lens-basis-text / --basis-text: the exact words "
            f"of the figure, its heading or its study's participants that name the group. Nothing was written.")
    if not re.search(r"\w", text):
        raise Refusal(f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} holds no letter or digit, so it names no one. "
                      f"Nothing was written.")
    if basis == "named_in_text":
        where = f"the figure's claim_text, or a file saved for {ref_id}"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id)
    elif basis == "context":
        where = f"the figure's claim_text, its source_section, or a file saved for {ref_id}"
        found = (_as_whole_words(text, claim_text) or _as_whole_words(text, source_section)
                 or _saved_text_has(text, ref_id))
    elif basis == "heading":
        where = "the figure's source_section (its heading)"
        found = _as_whole_words(text, source_section)
    else:
        where = f"the study_population of an evidence_population_match row for {ref_id}"
        found = any(_as_whole_words(text, r[0]) for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT study_population FROM evidence_population_match WHERE source_ref=?", (ref_id,)))
    if not found:
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: the warrant {text!r} (basis {basis}) is not, on word boundaries, in {where}. A link "
            f"rests on words the source holds, never on memory (CLAUDE.md 5(c)); a basis names where to look: "
            f"named_in_text the claim text or the source's saved file, heading the source_section, "
            f"study_participants the graded study_population, context the claim text, the source_section or the "
            f"source's saved file (its scope, application or purpose clause). Nothing was written.")
    return text, reason


def _refuse_all_by_context(basis, identity_codes, context):
    """`ALL` is not an identity (OD-31: "ALL leaves the identity lens"), so a judged context link never names it."""
    if basis == "context" and "ALL" in (identity_codes or ()):
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: --identity ALL by basis context: ALL is a scope marker, not a group (OD-31: grep -n -F "
            f"\"OD-31: a provision that names no one\" references/project-standards.md). Write the groups the clause "
            f"serves, or no identity. Nothing was written.")


def _write_lens_link(conn, extraction_id: int, col: str, code: str, basis: str, basis_text, session: str,
                     basis_reason=None) -> int:
    """INSERT one live link and return its link_id. The caller has checked the code and the warrant."""
    row = {"extraction_id": extraction_id, col: code, "basis": basis, "basis_text": basis_text,
           "basis_reason": basis_reason, **dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "extraction_lens_links", session)}
    return conn.execute(
        f"INSERT INTO extraction_lens_links ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
        list(row.values())).lastrowid


------
def _observed_source(conn, observation_id, attestation, verb):
    """The observation route's reading of a form, one home for add-alias and add-term
    --from-observation (T-028): the observation joined to its source, and the refusal of
    `instrument` for a source outside the regulatory stratum (derived from the tier ladder)."""
    obs = conn.execute(
        "SELECT o.observation_id, o.ref_id, o.surface_form, o.language, o.locator, "
        "o.context_quote, o.notes, e.jurisdiction, e.tier, e.evidence_type, e.scope "
        "FROM observed_terms o "
        "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = o.ref_id WHERE o.observation_id = ?",
        (observation_id,)).fetchone()
    if obs is None:
        raise Refusal(f"{verb}: observation {observation_id}: no such observed term.")
    if attestation == "instrument" and (obs["evidence_type"], obs["scope"]) not in _regulatory_pairs():
        raise Refusal(
            f"{verb}: --attestation instrument needs a source in the regulatory "
            f"stratum (a code, national framework or international standard); "
            f"{obs['ref_id']} is tier {obs['tier']}, evidence_type "
            f"{obs['evidence_type']!r}. Use other_source (the default), or the base "
            f"route with the instrument's own URL and clause. Nothing was written.")
    return obs


def _observed_quote(obs, verb):
    """(note, None) when the observation's quote contains its phrase and is in a file saved for its
    source (or carries VERBATIM-EXEMPT), else (None, the refusal's text). One standard for an attested
    form read from an observation: add-alias refuses on the text; add-term --from-observation writes
    the form `unrecorded` and says so (T-028)."""
    oid = obs["observation_id"]
    quote = obs["context_quote"] or ""
    kind, where, inside = _retrieval_log().classify_observation(
        obs["surface_form"], quote, obs["notes"], obs["ref_id"])
    if not quote.strip() or not inside:
        return None, (
            f"{verb}: observation {oid} carries no context quote that "
            f"contains its phrase, so nothing attests the phrase was seen. Observe the "
            f"sighting again with --locator and --context-quote (db.py observe-term), "
            f"adjudicate it, and alias from that observation.")
    if kind not in ("scoped", "exempt"):
        return None, (
            f"{verb}: observation {oid}'s quote is not in a file saved for "
            f"{obs['ref_id']} ({where}), so 'source-attested' would be untrue. Register "
            f"the source's text (scripts/research/full_text.py) and observe the sighting "
            f"from it, or record why no artefact can carry it (observe-term "
            f"--verbatim-exempt). Nothing was written.")
    return (f"source-attested: observation {oid}, {obs['ref_id']} at "
            f"{obs['locator']!r}; " + (f"quote verified in {where.split(',')[0]}"
                                      if kind == "scoped" else
                                      "the observation's quote is VERBATIM-EXEMPT")), None


def add_alias(term_id: str, observation_id: int, alias_type: str, session: str,
              dry_run: bool = False, *, alias: str = None, language: str = None,
              jurisdiction: str = None, source_url: str = None, source_page: str = None,
-----
def set_parameter_direction(*, parameter_id: int, direction: str, rationale: str,
                           session: str, ref_id: str = None, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record which way is BETTER FOR A DISABLED PERSON on this parameter.

    THE JUDGMENT THE ENGINE CANNOT MAKE, and the one it has been blocked on since
    2026-07-21. The most-accommodating rule (evidence-architecture.md, owner directive,
    Option A) says a determination anchors on the best-for-the-user value "read per the
    parameter's accessibility direction -- the widest minimum corridor, but the LOWEST
    maximum threshold height and the GENTLEST maximum ramp slope". Which of those a
    parameter is cannot be derived from its name, its unit, or its values: it is a fact
    about what the parameter means for a person, and somebody has to state it.

    So this is CLAUDE.md rule 8's other half in one verb. The vocabulary comes from the
    schema (`dbcore.check_declared`), the answer is a judgment, and the WARRANT is required
    beside it -- a direction with no stated reason is an assertion about disabled people's
    needs with nothing behind it, and the schema refuses that pair too (migration 078).

    `contested` IS AN ANSWER, not a refusal to answer. DR-2026-07-21 section 5: where the
    direction is population-contested -- flush thresholds aid wheeled mobility but remove
    the tactile cues cane users rely on, brighter light aids low vision but harms
    photosensitive users -- most-accommodating selection is INAPPLICABLE and no single value
    is anchored. Recording `contested` is what stops the engine silently picking a winner
    between two populations; leaving the field NULL would let a later session mistake "not
    yet examined" for "nothing to see".

    RE-STATING A DIRECTION IS REFUSED. The direction conditions every determination already
    computed for the parameter, so changing it silently re-points those determinations at a
    rule they were not computed under. Retire the parameter or open a decision; do not
    overwrite.
    """
    if not (rationale or "").strip():
        raise Refusal(
            "--rationale is required: a direction is a claim about what serves disabled "
            "people on this parameter, and one with no stated reason cannot be reviewed, "
            "disputed or superseded. The schema refuses the pair too (migration 078).")
    # FROM AN ADMITTED SOURCE, NEVER HAND-SET (ledger 2026-10-30, ACTION 6). The source
    # the direction was read from is a column (base_parameters.direction_ref_id, migration
    # 122), and it must hold an extraction for this parameter: a direction is read out of
    # what a document says about the quantity, not recalled. A walk-through on 2026-11-06
    # recorded a direction whose rationale was "no admitted source read".
    ref_id = dbcore.fold_ref(ref_id) if ref_id else None
    if not ref_id:
        raise Refusal(
            "--ref-id is required: the direction is recorded FROM an admitted source "
            "(ledger 2026-10-30, ACTION 6), never hand-set. Name the evidence_sources.ref_id "
            "whose extraction for this parameter states which way is better.")
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT p.parameter_id, t.canonical_en, p.accessibility_direction, "
            "p.direction_rationale FROM base_parameters p JOIN terms t "
            "ON t.term_id = p.term_id WHERE p.parameter_id = ?", [parameter_id]).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"parameter_id {parameter_id}: no such parameter. Mint one from a term "
                f"first: db.py add-parameter --term-id TERM-NNN --quantity-kind K --quantity-kind-quote Q --quantity-kind-source-url U --quantity-kind-source-page P --session ...")
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "evidence_sources", "ref_id", ref_id):
            raise Refusal(f"--ref-id {ref_id} is not an admitted source. The direction is "
                          f"read from a document this project holds; admit it first.")
        if not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions WHERE ref_id=? AND "
                            "parameter_id=? AND retired_at IS NULL", (ref_id, parameter_id)).fetchone():
            raise Refusal(
                f"--ref-id {ref_id} holds no extraction for parameter {parameter_id}, so "
                f"nothing it states about this quantity is on record. Extract the finding "
                f"that gives the direction (db.py add-extraction --figure-role finding ...) "
                f"first; then the direction points at it.")
        if row["accessibility_direction"]:
            raise Refusal(
                f"parameter {parameter_id} ({row['canonical_en']!r}) already carries "
                f"direction {row['accessibility_direction']!r}: "
                f"{row['direction_rationale']!r}.\nA direction conditions every "
                f"determination computed for the parameter, so overwriting it silently "
                f"re-points those at a rule they were not computed under. If it is wrong, "
                f"that is a decision (governance/decision-protocol.md), not an amendment.")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "base_parameters", "accessibility_direction",
                              direction, "set-parameter-direction")
        stamp = dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "base_parameters", session)
        sets = ["accessibility_direction = ?", "direction_rationale = ?", "direction_ref_id = ?"]
        vals = [direction, rationale.strip(), ref_id]
        for k, v in stamp.items():
            if k.startswith("updated"):
                sets.append(f"{k} = ?")
                vals.append(v)
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", vals + [parameter_id])
        return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "canonical_en": row["canonical_en"],
                "accessibility_direction": direction, "direction_rationale": rationale.strip(),
                "direction_ref_id": ref_id, "dry_run": dry_run}

===== base_units
CREATE TABLE base_units (
    unit                TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (length(trim(unit)) > 0 AND unit = trim(unit)),
    kind_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES base_quantity_kinds(kind_id),
    factor_numerator    INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (factor_numerator > 0),
    factor_denominator  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (factor_denominator > 0),
    figure_form         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (figure_form IN ('number', 'ratio')),
    system              TEXT CHECK (system IS NULL OR system IN ('metric', 'inch-foot')),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT
)
===== v_scan_ledger
CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a live (not retired, migration 158) non-absent extraction exists for the pair
--                        (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only live claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent' AND x.retired_at IS NULL) THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent' AND x.retired_at IS NULL) THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id
===== v_reading_owed
CREATE VIEW v_reading_owed AS
-- v_reading_owed: the (source, parameter) pairs whose reading is owed. One row per pair of v_scan_ledger that no FULL
-- reading covers (text_scope is the strongest covering reading's; NULL when none covers) and that the ledger does not
-- read BLOCKED. A partial, fragment or abstract reading covers nothing here, as in the ledger. Written once: the verb
-- `db.py defer-reading` asks it whether a deferral is allowed and v_deferred_acts asks it whether one still stands.
SELECT ref_id, parameter_id
  FROM v_scan_ledger
 WHERE COALESCE(text_scope, '') <> 'full'
   AND status <> 'BLOCKED'
===== source_scans
CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.
    file_sha256         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(file_sha256) = 64),
    -- Whether the open pass (quantities the catalogue lacks, plan section 3.4) was done
    -- in this reading.
    open_pass_done      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (open_pass_done IN (0, 1)),
    -- full-read: the text was read against the list. pre-screen: only a script listed
    -- where catalogue terms occur -- weaker, and v_scan_ledger says which it was.
    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    CHECK ((mode = 'targeted' AND target_parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (mode = 'catalogue' AND target_parameter_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_total IS NULL OR pages_read <= pages_total),
    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.
    CHECK (text_scope <> 'full' OR pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read = pages_total)
)
===== term_relations
CREATE TABLE "term_relations" (
    relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    from_term_id        TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    kind                TEXT NOT NULL
                        CHECK (kind IN ('broader', 'part of', 'element has parameter', 'element has provision',
                                        'adjacent', 'distinct')),
    to_term_id          TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    reason              TEXT CHECK (reason IS NULL OR length(trim(reason)) > 0),
    source_url          TEXT
    CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR (
        (source_url GLOB 'http://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*'
         OR source_url GLOB 'https://[^/' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')
        AND source_url NOT GLOB '*[' || char(32,9,10,13) || ']*')),
    source_page         TEXT
    CHECK (source_page IS NULL OR TRIM(source_page, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    source_line         INTEGER
    CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR (typeof(source_line) = 'integer' AND source_line > 0)),
    source_clause       TEXT
    CHECK (source_clause IS NULL OR TRIM(source_clause, char(32,9,10,13)) <> ''),
    ref_id              TEXT,                                               -- provenance only (OD-71): no foreign key
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    CHECK (from_term_id <> to_term_id),
    CHECK (source_url IS NOT NULL
           OR (source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL AND source_clause IS NULL)),
    CHECK (kind = 'distinct' OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL))),
    CHECK (kind <> 'distinct' OR reason IS NOT NULL),
    CHECK (kind <> 'distinct'
           OR CAST(substr(from_term_id, instr(from_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
              < CAST(substr(to_term_id, instr(to_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
           OR (CAST(substr(from_term_id, instr(from_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
               = CAST(substr(to_term_id, instr(to_term_id, '-') + 1) AS INTEGER)
               AND from_term_id < to_term_id)),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL) AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL)),
    CHECK (retired_at IS NULL OR (length(trim(retired_at)) > 0 AND length(trim(retired_by_session)) > 0
                                  AND length(trim(retirement_reason)) > 0))
)

def live_determinations_linked(conn, extraction_id, *, governing_only=False, proxy_only=False) -> list:
    """The LIVE determinations that carry extraction `extraction_id` in their provenance
    (`specification_extraction_links`), as sorted specification ids. Empty when none does.

    The row-level counterpart of `determinations_resting_on`, which answers for a source. Every
    extraction of a parameter is linked when a determination is written, graded by the part it
    played; a figure whose live lens links do not carry every code the cell states is linked
    `excluded` with the reason "not stated in this cell's lens (...)" (T-019, so that K02 holds). So
    "linked" means "an extraction of this parameter", NOT "read for this answer": a figure added to
    or amended under the parameter later is linked to every live cell of it, in or out of its lens.
    `governing_only` narrows it to the rows
    that supplied the value; `proxy_only` to determinations that rest on a proxy inference, the
    only ones whose marker reads `confirms` edges. LIVE means `retired_at IS NULL`, as there.
    """
    return [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
        "SELECT DISTINCT l.specification_id FROM specification_extraction_links l "
        "JOIN specifications s ON s.specification_id = l.specification_id "
        "WHERE l.extraction_id = ? AND s.retired_at IS NULL "
        + ("AND l.role = 'governing' " if governing_only else "")
        + ("AND s.rests_on_proxy_inference = 1 " if proxy_only else "")
        + "ORDER BY 1", (extraction_id,))]

T-137 and T-136 close the base to Korean and Japanese sources, T-138 item 2 turns judged lens links into falsely "named" ones, and T-138's own section 3 trips its stop condition. Task files are under `/home/user/guidebook/workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/`. Every probe was read-only or on a copy in my scratchpad, since deleted.

**1. T-137 §4 items 1–2 (shared figure reader) — HIGH, L.** The reader as specified refuses real non-English sources that today's digit test accepts. Simulated over live figures' `claim_text` against held units:
- KR: 15 rows hold a digit, 2 are read ("경사로의 기울기는 12분의 1 이하로", extraction 82).
- JP: 2 hold a digit, 0 read ("1/12", "8分の１").
- FI: 1 holds a digit, 0 read ("viisi prosenttia").
- Overall 185 → 141, but that total includes `N`, `points` and `degrees` rows whose kinds hold no unit yet.
- `幅は1200mm以上とする` reads nothing, because CJK characters count as `\w`.

The file's stated limit is also wrong: it says a decimal comma "is not read", but it is misread. `1,200 mm` gives 200 mm, `1,20 m` gives 20 m, `1 in = 25,4 mm` gives 4 mm, and `1 m = 1,000 mm` is refused.

**2. T-137 §4 item 1 (`add-unit`) — HIGH, L/W.** A unit spelled in the source's own script and equal to the canonical unit can never be added. On a copy, `мм`, `millimetres` and `毫米` at factor 1 all fail `ux_base_units_canonical`, and the file adds a matching refusal. `%` for `luminous_reflectance` fails the primary key (gradient holds it). Item 2 then makes the verbatim kind quote need the held spelling.

**3. T-136 §4 item 3 (relation quote) — HIGH, L.** `_as_whole_words` fails 8 of 9 real JA/KO observed phrases in their own quotes; six of those are plain substrings (`경사로` in `경사로의`). A relation found in a Japanese or Korean source is therefore refused with no route. The file names CJK only as a "known limit" to put in help text; Korean is hit too.

**4. T-138 §4 item 2 (item 19) — HIGH.** For 141 of 144 tier ≥ 4 figures, `context` with the first clause word (`Ramp`, `Rampenläufe`) is accepted today, and `named_in_text` accepts the same word for any identity (the docstring says it does not check that the words name the code). Followed literally, the refusal sends a judged link to `named_in_text`, where it is stored as "its own words name the users" and `basis_reason` is refused. This also reaches OD-47's ratified use of `context`.

- The reading that exposes a misreading precedes the retirement, so a second full reading is always owed (OD-23: "minimize duplicate reads").
- T138-09's "later full reading" cannot be built with the writers inside one minute.
- "Full-scope" is stricter than the ratified "no reading recorded after the retirement"; the file says so.

**7. T-136 §4 item 1 (item 13) — MEDIUM, worst case for the book.** The file is faithful to the ratified item, but what replaces "admitted source holding an extraction" is any quote with a letter plus any URL and page, and the direction is write-once. `x`, `https://example.org`, `n/a` fixes the direction every determination is selected by. `contested` must rest on one quote, though a contest is two sources.

**8. T-136 §4 item 2 — MEDIUM.** The phrase-in-quote test "becomes" a refusal on `add-term --from-observation`. Item 14 resolved "`unrecorded` otherwise"; this refusal is the author's.

**9. T-137 §4 item 3 against T-143 — MEDIUM.** The TEXT CHECK (digits and one `/`) cannot hold a tangent-governed bound. T-143 line 70 flags it as an open point; T-137 is silent.
